questions.question: In tennis, what is a score of zero called?
questions.explanation: Nobody is quite sure where it comes from, and in cricket a score of zero is called a duck.

questions.question: Which Grand Slam tennis tournament is played on grass in London?
questions.explanation: Players at Wimbledon have to dress almost entirely in white.

questions.question: In cricket, how many balls are bowled in a normal over?
questions.explanation: After each over, a different bowler takes over from the other end.

questions.question: Which British driver won the Formula 1 world championship in 2008 and again in 2014?
questions.explanation: Hamilton won his first title with McLaren and his second with Mercedes.

questions.question: In which sport do teams slide heavy stones across the ice while team-mates sweep in front of them?
questions.explanation: Britain's women won Olympic curling gold in 2002 with a last stone nicknamed the 'Stone of Destiny'.

questions.question: How many players does each side have on the pitch in a rugby union match?
questions.explanation: Rugby league teams have 13 players, and rugby sevens has, of course, seven.

questions.question: In darts, what is the highest score you can get with three darts?
questions.explanation: You need all three darts in the treble 20, which is worth 60 each.

questions.question: In snooker, how many points is the black ball worth?
questions.explanation: The black is the most valuable ball on the table; the pink is worth 6.

questions.question: England's women won the 2025 Rugby World Cup at Twickenham. What is the team's nickname?
questions.explanation: They beat Canada 33–13 in front of more than 81,000 fans, a record crowd for women's rugby.

questions.question: In 2021, which British 18-year-old won the US Open tennis after starting in the qualifying rounds?
questions.explanation: She won all ten of her matches without losing a single set.

questions.question: How many players from each team are on the court in a game of netball?
questions.explanation: Each player wears a bib with letters, like GS for goal shooter, showing where they are allowed to go.

questions.question: In golf, what is it called when you finish a hole in one shot fewer than par?
questions.explanation: Two under par is an eagle, and three under is an albatross.

questions.question: How many hurdles do the runners jump in a 110m hurdles race?
questions.explanation: Women run the 100m hurdles, and they also jump ten.

questions.question: England and Australia play cricket for a tiny trophy known as what?
questions.explanation: The little urn is said to hold the ashes of a burnt cricket bail, from England's tour of 1882–83.

questions.question: Keely Hodgkinson won Olympic gold in 2024 in which running race?
questions.explanation: That is two laps of the track, and she had won silver in the same race in Tokyo.

questions.question: In snooker, how many points is a 'maximum break'?
questions.explanation: It takes all 15 reds, each followed by the black, then all six colours in order.

questions.question: In 2013, who became the first British man to win the Wimbledon singles since Fred Perry in 1936?
questions.explanation: Murray beat Novak Djokovic in straight sets in the final, then won Wimbledon again in 2016.

questions.question: Jonny Wilkinson's late drop goal won England the 2003 Rugby World Cup final against which country?
questions.explanation: He kicked it with his weaker right foot in the last minute of extra time in Sydney.

questions.question: Which golfer won the 1997 Masters aged 21, by a record 12 strokes?
questions.explanation: He became the youngest Masters champion and the first of African-American heritage.

questions.question: By the end of 2025, which man had won the most Grand Slam tennis singles titles?
questions.explanation: Djokovic moved past Rafael Nadal's total of 22 when he won the 2023 French Open, and finished 2025 with 24.

questions.question: Which country won the first Rugby World Cup, in 1987?
questions.explanation: The All Blacks beat France in the final in Auckland; New Zealand co-hosted with Australia.

questions.question: In darts, what is the fewest number of darts needed to finish a game of 501?
questions.explanation: A nine-darter is the perfect leg, usually two 180s followed by a 141 checkout.

questions.question: Which British driver won the 1996 Formula 1 title, as his father had in 1962 and 1968?
questions.explanation: Damon and Graham Hill were the first father and son both to become Formula 1 world champions.

questions.question: Which Australian batsman finished his Test career with an average of 99.94?
questions.explanation: He needed just four runs in his final innings in 1948 to average 100, but was out second ball for a duck.

questions.question: In which year did Virginia Wade win the Wimbledon singles, in the Queen's Silver Jubilee summer?
questions.explanation: The Queen was in the Royal Box to watch her lift the trophy.

questions.question: In 2021, who became the first woman to ride the winner of the Grand National?
questions.explanation: She won on Minella Times, a few weeks after becoming the leading jockey at the Cheltenham Festival.

questions.question: Roger Bannister ran the first mile in under four minutes in 1954 in which city?
questions.explanation: He ran 3 minutes 59.4 seconds at the Iffley Road track.

questions.question: At which Scottish course was the very first Open Championship played, in 1860?
questions.explanation: Only eight golfers took part, and the prize was a red leather belt rather than a claret jug.

questions.question: Who became the first Formula 1 world champion, in 1950?
questions.explanation: Farina drove for Alfa Romeo and won the very first championship race, at Silverstone.

questions.question: In December 2019, who became the first woman to win a match at the PDC World Darts Championship?
questions.explanation: She beat Ted Evetts at Alexandra Palace, then won again to reach the third round.

questions.question: How many feathers does a proper badminton shuttlecock have?
questions.explanation: The feathers usually come from geese or ducks and are fixed into a little rounded cork base.

questions.question: The sport of rugby takes its name from what?
questions.explanation: It is named after Rugby School in Warwickshire, where the game grew up in the 1800s.

questions.question: In tennis, what is it called when a serve is so good that the other player cannot even touch it?
questions.explanation: The fastest serves in top tennis fly at well over 200 kilometres an hour.

questions.question: In the Tour de France, what colour jersey does the rider leading the race wear?
questions.explanation: It is yellow because the newspaper that started the race, L'Auto, was printed on yellow paper.

questions.question: When basketball was invented in 1891, what did players throw the ball into?
questions.explanation: The baskets still had their bottoms in, so someone had to fetch the ball out after every score.

questions.question: How many holes are there in a full round of golf?
questions.explanation: Scotland's most famous old course once had 22 holes, until some were joined together in 1764 to make 18.

questions.question: In North America, which sport's top prize is the Stanley Cup?
questions.explanation: It is named after Lord Stanley, a British governor general of Canada, who gave the cup in 1892.

questions.question: Sumo wrestling is the national sport of which country?
questions.explanation: Before a bout, the wrestlers throw salt into the ring to make it pure.

questions.question: In cricket, what do the letters LBW stand for?
questions.explanation: A batter can be out LBW if the ball hits their leg when it would have gone on to hit the stumps.

questions.question: How many players are on each team in a polo match?
questions.explanation: The riders swap to fresh ponies during a match, because galloping about soon tires them out.
